study type: Retrospective comparative study using national registries
exposure: 1 mg vitamin K orally at birth followed by daily oral 25 µg vitamin K
1 mg vitamin K orally at birth followed by daily oral 150 µg vitamin K
Single intramuscular (IM) 2 mg vitamin K at birth
cohort: The study cohort consisted of breastfed infants with unrecognized cholestasis, such as biliary atresia, identified through national registries in the Netherlands and Denmark.
finding: Oral vitamin K prophylactic regimens (either 25 µg or 150 µg daily after 1 mg oral at birth) failed to prevent VKDB in breastfed infants with unrecognized biliary atresia, whereas a single 2 mg intramuscular dose of vitamin K at birth was highly effective.
